title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 61-63). A 'disposition' on a set E is a symmetric relation x|o|y, which I read as orthogonality or disjointness. For subsets, A|o|B means every a in A satisfies a|o|b for every b in B. The operator cosupp°(A) (also written inv° or conv°) is the set of elements orthogonal to all of A, i.e. A^⊥. The operator supp°(A) is the double orthogonal A^⊥⊥, the 'support' or closure of A. Σ_E is the lattice of closed subsets; for an irreflexive relation it is a complete ortholattice. In modern terms (E, |o|) is an orthogonality space or orthoset in the sense of Dacey and Foulis–Randall. A map α: E→E' is 'compatible with dispositions' if x|o|y implies α(x)|o|α(y). It induces ᾱ on subsets and α_*: Σ_E→Σ_E', A ↦ closure of α(A).

The problem being served: when does α_* commute with orthocomplementation C? Equivalently, when does formula (**) hold: x'|o|ᾱ(B) and y'|o|ᾱ(C) imply x'|o|y'?

On p. 61, the 'tautological disposition' (x|o|y iff x≠y, so Σ = all subsets, Boolean) gives a counterexample. Compatibility then means α is injective, but α_* commutes with complements only if α is bijective. This page opens by finishing that sentence.

Grothendieck then adds a 'correspondence in the opposite direction' β: E'→P(E), equivalently a union-preserving map β̄: P(E')→P(E). He imposes condition (*): ᾱ(β(x')) ⊂ supp°({x'}).

Argument:
1. If x'|o|ᾱ(B), then {x'}^⊥⊥ ⊥ ᾱ(B), hence ᾱ(β(x')) |o| ᾱ(B).
2. If ᾱ is 'faithful' (ᾱ(S)|o|ᾱ(T) implies S|o|T), then β(x')|o|B.
3. Apply this to (B, x') and to (C, y') with C = cosupp°(B) = B^⊥. This gives β(x')|o|B and β(y')|o|B^⊥, i.e. β(y') ⊂ B^⊥⊥ = supp°(B).
4. Hence β(x')|o|β(y'), and so ᾱβ(x')|o|ᾱβ(y').

On p. 63 Grothendieck sees that to get x'|o|y' he needs supp°(ᾱβ(x')) = supp°({x'}). He then picks the optimal β = α*, with α*(x') = {x : α(x) ∈ supp°{x'}}, a right-adjoint-type preimage of the closure of a point. His final hypotheses are:
(i) supp°(ᾱα*(x')) = supp°{x'}, a surjectivity substitute;
(ii) faithful compatibility, x|o|y iff α(x)|o|α(y).
This is an elementary study of morphisms of orthogonality spaces that preserve orthocomplementation on the closure lattices.
errors: The displayed equivalence x'|o|ᾱ(B) ⟺ ᾱ(β(x'))|o|ᾱ(B) only holds in the ⇒ direction under (*). The ⇐ direction needs x' ∈ supp°(ᾱβ(x')), i.e. the equality of supports that Grothendieck himself identifies on the next page as hypothesis (i). Only ⇒ is used in the argument on this page, so the reasoning survives.
'Fidélité' of ᾱ is used for subsets (ᾱ(S)|o|ᾱ(T) ⇒ S|o|T) but is not defined precisely here. On p. 63 it is replaced by pointwise faithful compatibility (ii), which implies the subset version.

ideas.what: Symmetric 'disposition' relation on a set, with Galois closure A ↦ A^⊥⊥ giving a complete ortholattice of closed subsets
Condition for an induced map of closure lattices to commute with orthocomplement: a reverse correspondence β = α* with support equality and faithful (reflecting) orthogonality
ideas.modern_name: adjointable / orthogonality-reflecting morphisms of orthosets; Galois-adjoint pair between ortholattices

ideas.what: Counterexample showing that injectivity (mere compatibility) is insufficient; in the tautological (Boolean) case bijectivity is needed

missed.claim: Grothendieck in 1986 develops, independently and in his own vocabulary ('disposition', supp°, cosupp°), the morphism theory of orthogonality spaces. He arrives at an adjoint-type reverse map α* and a 'faithful compatibility' condition, close to the adjointable maps of orthosets later studied in quantum-logic foundations. This is a historical curiosity rather than a new result.
missed.quote: On va supposer donnée une correspondance en sens inverse E' →β P(E) ... (*) ∀x'∈E', ᾱ(β(x')) ⊂ supp°_{E'}({x'})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck engaging with orthocomplemented-lattice structures, a topic absent from his known corpus. It might be of interest to historians, but the mathematics itself is elementary and covered by the existing literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is elementary lattice/Galois-connection reasoning about orthogonality relations, with standard modern counterparts. Its only interest is that Grothendieck pursued orthoset-like structures in 1986 notes, which is unusual but not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: The ⟺ in 'x' |o| ᾱ(B) ⟺ ᾱ(β(x'))|o|ᾱ(B)' is clearly drawn in the image, so it is transcribed correctly, though it is mathematically only ⇒.
'supp°_{E'}' on this page appears consistent with the next page's 'sup-pr°'. It probably denotes the same support operator, 'supp°'.
The marginal note is roughly 'NB Si fidélité (*) est fort justifié, cf. p. 2[?]'; the reading is uncertain.
'β(y') |o| C = cosupp°(B)' should be read as: β(y')|o|C, where C = cosupp°(B).
